1. Read the Crime, Waste and neighbour-list files into pandas DataFrames.

2. Merge Crime and Waste columns on “borough”; keep only the 33 unique borough rows.

3. Handle missing data: drop any borough that has a missing value in either Crime_value (1 row) or Waste_value (1 row).  
   • Record the remaining N boroughs.  
   • When a borough is dropped, also delete every edge in the neighbour list that contains that borough so that no weights refer to a missing observation.

4. Build an N × N binary contiguity matrix W where W[i,j] = 1 if borough i is listed as a neighbour of borough j (exclude self-links).  
   • Row-standardise: divide each non-zero row by its row sum so that every row sums to 1.  
   • Compute S0 = Σ_i Σ_j W[i,j] (which now equals N because of row standardisation but store the exact value produced by code).

5. Standardise the two variables:  
   z_crime = (Crime – mean(Crime)) / std(Crime)  
   z_waste = (Waste – mean(Waste)) / std(Waste)

6. Compute the observed Lee’s L statistic for bivariate spatial association:  
   L_obs = (1/S0) · Σ_i Σ_j W[i,j] · z_crime[i] · z_waste[j]

7. Significance testing (permutation):  
   a. Fix z_crime.  
   b. For ≥999 iterations (≥500 required, choose 999), randomly permute z_waste between boroughs, recompute L_perm each time.  
   c. Build the null distribution of L_perm values.  
   d. Two-sided p-value = ( (#|L_perm| ≥ |L_obs|) + 1 ) / (iterations + 1).

8. Classify the spatial relationship:  
   • If p < 0.05 and L_obs > 0 ⇒ “POSITIVE”.  
   • If p < 0.05 and L_obs < 0 ⇒ “NEGATIVE”.  
   • Otherwise ⇒ “NOT SIGNIFICANT”.

9. Report the conclusion with the exact numeric L_obs and p produced by the computation.

Missing-value policy summarised: rows containing any NA in Crime_value or Waste_value are dropped; their neighbour links are removed before weight construction.

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# ------------------ 1. LOAD DATA ------------------
DATA_PATH = "chunks_csv/bivariate/bivariate_2023_crime_waste.csv"
ADJ_PATH  = "chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv"

df = pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJ_PATH)

# ------------------ 2. DROP MISSING VALUES ------------------
df_clean = df.dropna(subset=["Crime_value", "Waste_value"]).reset_index(drop=True)
kept_boroughs = set(df_clean["borough"])

# restrict adjacency list to kept boroughs only
adj_clean = adj[adj["borough"].isin(kept_boroughs) & adj["neighbor"].isin(kept_boroughs)]

# ------------------ 3. BUILD WEIGHT MATRIX ------------------
boroughs = df_clean["borough"].tolist()
idx_map = {b:i for i,b in enumerate(boroughs)}
n = len(boroughs)

W = np.zeros((n, n), dtype=float)

for _, row in adj_clean.iterrows():
    i = idx_map[row["borough"]]
    j = idx_map[row["neighbor"]]
    W[i, j] = 1          # directional
    W[j, i] = 1          # ensure symmetry / undirected

# remove self links (just to be safe)
np.fill_diagonal(W, 0)

# row-standardise
row_sums = W.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
nonzero_rows = row_sums.flatten() > 0
W[nonzero_rows] = W[nonzero_rows] / row_sums[nonzero_rows]

S0 = W.sum()

# ------------------ 4. STANDARDISE VARIABLES ------------------
crime = df_clean["Crime_value"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
waste = df_clean["Waste_value"].to_numpy(dtype=float)

z_crime = (crime - crime.mean()) / crime.std(ddof=1)
z_waste = (waste - waste.mean()) / waste.std(ddof=1)

# ------------------ 5. OBSERVED LEE'S L ------------------
cross = np.outer(z_crime, z_waste)          # z_x[i] * z_y[j]
L_obs = (W * cross).sum() / S0

# ------------------ 6. PERMUTATION TEST ------------------
n_perm = 999
rng = np.random.default_rng(seed=42)

L_perm = np.empty(n_perm)

for k in range(n_perm):
    permuted = rng.permutation(z_waste)
    cross_perm = np.outer(z_crime, permuted)
    L_perm[k] = (W * cross_perm).sum() / S0

# two–sided p-value
p_value = (np.sum(np.abs(L_perm) >= abs(L_obs)) + 1) / (n_perm + 1)

# ------------------ 7. CLASSIFY RESULT ------------------
if p_value < 0.05:
    direction = "POSITIVE" if L_obs > 0 else "NEGATIVE"
else:
    direction = "NOT SIGNIFICANT"

# ------------------ 8. OUTPUT ------------------
print(f"data_points_used = {n}")
print(f"FINAL ANSWER: {direction} (test statistic = {L_obs}, p = {p_value})")
